To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuromodulatory responses to neuropeptides vary with receptor and ion channel expression levels, and that this variation can be characterized by a discrete set of response phenotypes.

1) the expression of a neuropeptidergic receptor and multiple ion channel proteins in a single cell determines the neuromodulatory phenotype of the cell, and 2) the relative contributions of the neuropeptideric receptor and ion channel expression to the neuromodulated excitability of a neuron depends on the biophysical state of the ion channels.

the response to neuromodulatory stimulation is a complex function of receptor expression and ion channel levels, and that the response phenotype depends on both the receptor and ion channel expression levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between molecular variability and cellular responses to neuropedutic stimuli.
the relationship between molecular variability and cellular function.
the effects of molecular variability on cellular excitability and neuropedutary response phenotypes.

our study showed that the molecular variability in the levels of neuropeptide receptors and ion channels can elicit a discrete switch in neuromodulatory phenotypes, with the relative contribution of each molecular component to the response phenotype depending on the biophysical state of the neuron.
our results show that the neuromodulatory effect on neuronal excitability is dependent on the expression of multiple ion channels and neuropeptide receptor.
the response of a neuron to neuromodulatory input is determined by a complex interplay between the molecular variability of receptor expression and biophysically active ion channel levels.

a tunable switch, which is formed by a molecular variability, elicits a tunably switchable neuromodulatory responses.
